issue.body:
- `nvim --version`: NVIM v0.4.0-1760-g7ed212262
- `vim -u DEFAULTS` (version: 8.0) behaves differently? yes
- Operating system/version: WIndows 10
- Terminal name/version: nvim-qt

Using :jumps, calling getjumplist() or using ctrl-o when the topmost jumplist entry is on the current line deletes that jumplist entry.

### Steps to reproduce using `nvim -u NORC`

- Generate a file for testing, e.g. `100ia<esc>yy5p`

Reproduction:
- Create a jumplist entry with m'
- Move somewhere else on the same line
- use ctrl-o

### Actual behaviour
We delete the jumplist entry on the current line and jump to some previous jumplist entry.

### Expected behaviour
Jump back to the marked location on the current line. Create a jump point in the location we used ctrl-o at which will replace the jumplist entry since we can only have one jumplist entry per line.
(Whether this behavior is intuitive is debatable but it's what vim and older neovim versions do)

issue.title: jumplist: alleviate *, # command regression

repository.name: neovim
repository.description: Vim-fork focused on extensibility and usability

issue.body:
This is a partial resolution to #9874. It improves the situation but I believe it
reveals that the approach in #9805 is too naive.

---

Commit 35362495c ("jumplist: avoid extra tail entry #9805", 2019-04-02)
introduced a regression where, when the * or # command leaves the cursor
in the same line, the jumplist entry is erroneously erased. In addition
to interactive use, this breaks mappings like

    nnoremap * *<C-O>

The cursor remains in the same line when

1. the cursor is outside of a word boundary;
2. the searched-for word occurs next time in the same line; or
3. the searched-for word is unique.

Only erase the jumplist entry when both the cursor line and column
position are unchanged. This still leaves case #3 confusingly broken but
hopefully it's enough to salvage interactive use -- why "jump back" when
the cursor doesn't move? -- even if it turns out to be insufficient for
aforementioned mapping.

The slightly more clumsy alternative mapping of

    nnoremap * *``

doesn't help: `` updates the jumplist, too, so unique keywords move the
cursor to the position before the * command instead of staying in place.
If that command is used on a unique keyword after being used on a
non-unique keyword, that position is the "next match of the searched-for
word" from the previous usage.

body:
> it doesn't make sense to me at all that the behavior changes depending on the cursor position

I perceived it not as an intended change in behaviour but as a way to emulate that a particular event (record a jumplist entry) does not occur, only it uses incomplete (and insufficient) information.

This regression breaks one of my oldest mappings, and introduces an inconvenient exception to muscle memory for anyone that uses `*` (`#`) frequently without that mapping. It's bad enough that I'm not entirely convinced my slight improvement in #12607 is good enough for me. At the very least, I think this warrants a bigger mention in `vim-differences` than just

>   The jumplist avoids useless/phantom jumps.

Does that mean that * should be able to add multiple columns on the same line to the jump list? This isn't working for me at the moment (v0.9 and compiled from master). I tried to understand what is going on in #21874, but couldn't really see how it should affect this issue here. Thanks a lot for any info :)

issue.title: Leap to same line not added to jumplist
issue.body:
Hi,
I'm working a lot in LaTeX code with long lines, and often I leap to a position in the same line (which may be wrapped many times, so doesn't feel like the same line). When I try to jump back to my previous location before the leap, I get to some previous jump position, as a leap to the same line doesn't seem to be added to the jumplist. It would be great to have this feature!
